card.name: Long Drum Dance
card.tagline: Yao dancers leap with meter-long waist drums
card.profile: The Long Drum Dance (長鼓舞, Changgu) is a folk dance of the Yao people popular in Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan and other Yao areas, performed at festivals, harvests and weddings (TravelChina). Dancers wear and beat a drum about a meter (roughly 4 chi) long, performing vigorous, acrobatic movements imitating climbing, building houses and fighting tigers. It is rooted in the Yao ritual sacrifice to King Pan (Panhu).
card.insight: Yao Changgu was inscribed on China's second batch of national intangible cultural heritage in 2008 and inspired the famous orchestral composition 'Dance of the Yao People' (1952) (English Wikipedia; dotdotnews).
card.image_significance: Two long drums, one name. A representative image shows precise formation with fans, sleeves or masks and refined stagecraft — Yanbian/Yao, China.
card.sacred_note: Some drum dances, such as the Ojibwe drum dance, involve a 'dream drum' that is considered sacred and may be treated as a living thing.
